newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Lombard NatWest profits jump, forecast good.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Lombard NatWest profits jump, forecast good.

text.p: Cyprus-based Lombard NatWest on Monday announced a 100 percent jump in pre-tax profits for 1996, with prospects for the coming year equally good, bank officials said.
Profit before tax for the Cyprus-based bank reached 3.28 million Cyprus pounds ($6.65 million) for the year ended September 30 1996, compared to 1.64 million pounds recorded in 1995.

"If we exclude one-off items associated with the liquidation of shares then profit before tax reached 2.27 million, a rise of 39 percent on 1995," said Michael Colocassides, chairman of the bank's board of directors.
"These results reaffirm the reputation of Lombard NatWest as a fast-growing, profitable bank," he told a news conference.
"We expect to continue our healthy growth with satisfactory results in the coming year," he said.
The National Westminster Bank owns 75 percent of Lombard NatWest in Cyprus, which started offering a full range of banking services on the island in 1991.
Colocassides said the bank was currently strengthening its treasury and foreign exchange operations, and had started to offer trustee services in association with Coutts.
He said the bank was working on introducing private banking services in the near future.
The bank has five main branches and nineteen sub-branches and tourist sub-offices. It employs a workforce of 250. ($=0.49 pounds)
